title: Thorn and Crown
premise: Quentin Pemberton, a hedge-witch's runaway apprentice, hides in a valley where magic cannot follow—until the crown's witch-hunt reaches even there, and his master is dragged to the court beneath the mountain. Following the hunters' trail, Quentin falls in with a found family of smugglers and a disgraced royal inquisitor who knows the court's secrets: the crown's power is fed by souls sold to the thing sleeping under the mountain, and the last dragon's dying fire is the only force that can unmake those bargains. Quentin must steal back his master's soul—and his own, unknowingly sold years ago—before the dragon-fire gutters out. In the end he chooses truth over loyalty to his found family's code of silence, exposing the crown's bargain and freeing the valley, though the cost is the magic he was born with.
about_author: Odile Ravensworth is the pen name of a former archivist who claims to have catalogued three thousand unsent letters and stolen one idea from each. She writes fantasy about people the histories forgot, from a drafty attic full of maps that argue with each other.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. He tends bees and buries his gift deep, hiding in the magic-dead valley where his master Maren raised him after he fled his apprenticeship. When royal hunters arrive asking after 'the hedge-witch of Hollowmere,' Quentin's careful invisibility shatters. Emotional beat: the dread of a past catching up.

chapters.title: Iron and Ivy
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The hunters take Maren; Quentin, using a scrap of forbidden craft, escapes into the hills with Maren's grimoire and a debt he can't name. He meets Brannock's smuggling crew at a river crossing. Emotional beat: guilt and the first fragile taste of belonging.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Oath
chapters.summary: Brannock's POV. The crew—Brannock, twins Sef and Ila, and the taciturn cook Oda—debate what to do with the boy who carries a hunted book. Quentin earns his place by hiding the whole camp with a working no one his age should manage. Emotional beat: found family offered, at a price of secrets.

chapters.title: What the Inquisitor Knew
chapters.summary: Serah Vane's POV. A disgraced royal inquisitor, Serah intercepts the crew and reveals the court beneath the mountain buys souls to feed the crown's power—and that Maren's soul was sold within a day of capture. She offers to guide them in exchange for passage to the dragon's last fire. Emotional beat: uneasy alliance, truth as currency.

chapters.title: Road of Ash
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The company travels through burned villages where the hunt has already passed; Quentin heals a dying child and nearly exposes them all. Sef accuses him of valuing magic over the crew's safety. Emotional beat: loyalty fraying under the weight of conscience.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Serah's POV. Infiltrating the mountain court through an inquisitor's forgotten door, Serah sees her former order's rot firsthand and finds records of a second soul sold from Hollowmere years ago—Quentin's. Emotional beat: horror and the resolve to tell a truth that will hurt.

chapters.title: Sold Twice Over
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Serah confesses that Quentin's own soul was sold by Maren to save his life as a child. Quentin turns on the crew, then on Maren when they find her cell—she chose his survival over his freedom. Emotional beat: betrayal, and the question of what loyalty owes.

chapters.title: The Last Dragon-Fire
chapters.summary: Brannock's POV. Racing the gutters of the dragon's flame, the crew breaches the deep vault where souls are kept as embers in glass. The dragon, ancient and nearly spent, will unmake one bargain—only one. Emotional beat: sacrifice chosen, not demanded.

chapters.title: Crown of Embers
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Climax. Quentin gives up his own reclaimed soul-ember to the dragon to unmake the crown's founding bargain, toppling the court's power as the mountain shakes. Maren's soul returns to her; his magic burns out with the flame. Emotional beat: justice paid in the only coin he had.

chapters.title: Thorn and Crown
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV, coda. Magicless but alive, Quentin returns to a valley no longer hidden, where the crew has built a refuge for the hunted. Maren asks forgiveness; he offers a beginning instead of absolution. Emotional beat: quiet resolution—family chosen, truth told, and a life rebuilt without the gift.
